requirements.note: Newest first, grouped by day in inset-grouped sections; each header reads e.g. 'Oct 25, 2026 · $222.02', and the day total updates after edits (Oct 25 went to $226.47 after an edit).
A 'This Month' card at the top shows $5,269.70 and 'October 2026 · 86 expenses'. It updated correctly after add, edit and delete.

Sheet with amount (decimal pad), merchant, a category menu listing all 7 categories, a date picker defaulting to Oct 28, 2026 (today) and a note. The ✓ Save button stays disabled for -5, 0, non-numeric text or an empty merchant, with inline footer text ('Must be positive.', 'Enter a merchant.').
Tapping a row opens an Edit Expense sheet with every field filled in, and edits save. Swiping left shows a red Delete action, and tapping it removes the row and updates the totals.

Categories tab: month total, then categories largest first, each with expense count, '% of total', amount and a progress bar. Tapping one pushes a list of that category's transactions for the month, grouped by day.
All amounts show as $x,xxx.xx. The added expense, an edited amount and a deletion all survived relaunch.

bugs: Minor: the 'Must be positive.' error shows on a fresh, empty Add form before the user has typed anything.
tells: Category rows on the Categories screen are tappable and push a screen, but have no disclosure chevron.
While a row is swiped open for Delete, the whole row turns grey, as if it were selected.
Very stock and plain: transaction rows have no category icon or colour, and amounts are grey secondary text. Native, but a bit bare.
A.scroll: Smooth native collection-view scrolling across ~26 pages: slow drags, flings and fling-back to the top showed no blank or popping rows, and the pull past the top rubber-bands with the large title. Scroll position was kept after opening and cancelling an edit and after switching tabs.

requirements.note: Newest first, grouped by day with sticky headers ('Today' / 'Sun, Oct 25') and the day total right-aligned. Rows show a category icon, the note and a chevron.

A green 'This month · October 2026' card shows $5,269.70, the expense count, a category colour strip and a 'View breakdown' link that switches to the Categories tab. Totals updated correctly after add, edit and delete.

Sheet with a large $ amount field (decimal pad with a Done accessory), merchant, a category popup listing all 7 categories with icons, a date defaulting to today and an optional note. Save stays enabled; tapping it with an empty amount, -5 or a missing merchant brings up an alert ('Enter a positive amount', 'Add a merchant').
Tapping a row opens an Edit expense sheet with the fields filled in, and edits save. Swiping left shows a red Delete action that removes the row and updates the totals.

Categories tab: month card, then 'Where it went', largest first, each with an icon, count, amount, '% of total' and a coloured bar. Tapping one pushes that category's transactions for the month, grouped by day.
All amounts show as US currency. The added expense, an edited amount and a deletion all survived relaunch.

bugs: Editing an expense saved as 12.50 shows the amount as '12.5' in the field.
Share precision is inconsistent: '28.1% of total' and '14.4%' next to '14% of total'.
With the merchant keyboard up, the first tap on the Category row did nothing; it needed a second tap after dismissing the keyboard.
tells: Validation uses blocking alerts after Save, where iOS apps usually disable Save or show the error inline.

Custom cream and dark-green palette with a filled green Save pill and a text 'Cancel' pill. Branded rather than system tinted, though the system controls underneath (tables, liquid-glass tab bar, date picker, menus) are native.
At the largest text size, the left edge of the 'View breakdown' link text is clipped inside the green card ('V' and 'd' are cut off).
B.scroll: Smooth native table scrolling across ~36 pages with sticky day headers: flings and fling-back to the top showed no blank rows or popping, and pulling past the top reveals a search field. Position was mostly kept after opening and cancelling an edit (it shifted about 10 pt) and after switching tabs.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist correctly, with clean native lists and good dark-mode and Dynamic Type support. A is the more stock-looking app and validates more idiomatically (Save disabled, inline errors), but it looks bare. B adds category icons, notes in the rows, a search field, sticky headers and a breakdown link with a cohesive design, so it is the one I would rather use and ship, despite its alert-based validation and a few small formatting slips.
